newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Sonatrach studies buying into Portugal's EDP - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sonatrach studies buying into Portugal's EDP - paper.

text.p: Algerian state oil company Sonatrach is considering taking part in the partial privatisation of Portuguese electricity group EDP-Electricidade de Portugal, Sonatrach's director general was quoted as saying.
"We are making preliminary contacts," Nazim Zouioueche told Portuguese newspaper Diario de Noticias in a report from Algiers. He declined to give further details.
The Portuguese government plans to partially privatise EDP in the first half of 1997.

Zouioueche reaffirmed that Sonatrach was interested in taking a stake in Portuguese state-owned natural gas distributor Transgas. "We want 10 percent of Transgas, or at least five percent," he told the paper.

Secretary of State for Industry and Energy Jose Penedos told Reuters in July that the Portuguese government planned to open capital in Transgas to Sonatrach and possibly to other partners in the second half of 1997.
Transgas is building a natural gas pipeline due to be completed at the end of 1996. The pipeline will distribute gas from Algeria via Morocco to Spain and Portugal.
